how_it_behaves: Login may be followed by both a browser 'Save password?' panel and an OpenEMR Product Registration modal. The top-right global demographics search and entering 'First Last' in Patient Finder often return 'No matching records found' because patients are stored as 'Last, First' and the global search leaves a hidden filter; opening Finder from the top menu and searching the table by last name only is reliable. Similar names and even exact duplicate names can appear; when more than one row shows the exact same 'Last, First' name, open the first, topmost exact-matching row in the table so the choice is deterministic, and do not open a similar or look-alike name. Clicking a Patient Finder name can refresh back to an empty list, requiring the same exact name in the first matching row to be clicked again. Patient charts open on Dashboard; Demographics is below the fold and its External ID is the plan member ID. The blue patient name in the chart header is immediately followed by a parenthesised ID and a close 'x', which can make that name hard to read in isolation; the same patient name is repeated in plain black text after 'Medical Record Dashboard -' below the chart tabs, and that heading text is the reliable place to read the name from. The Issues page lists Medical Problems and Medications as collapsed rows with a '>' expander; expanded dates and comments can run past one screen. Reading the Issues list scrolls the page page by page, so when that read finishes the page is left scrolled toward its last page and rows collected from earlier pages are above the top of the screen and cannot be clicked from that screenshot; return to the top of the Issues page before expanding any row, then expand rows in the top-to-bottom order they were read, scrolling down a little at a time until each named title link and its '>' expander are both fully visible before clicking that expander, because expanding earlier rows also pushes later rows further down. The Medical Issues page opens as its own 'Patient Issues' tab and does not show the Dashboard, History, Issues chart navigation row that is visible on the Dashboard, so there is no 'Dashboard' link to click to get back from Issues, at any scroll position; the large blue patient name at the top-left of the header, beside the grey avatar icon and immediately before the parenthesised ID, remains visible on the Issues page and is the route back to that patient's Medical Record Dashboard. An expanded Issues block may show only 'Last Modified' and 'Comments' detail rows, with no begin, start or end date labels at all; such a block is still a fully expanded block and must be counted, with any date or other detail that is not shown recorded as not recorded rather than the whole block being discarded. Editing a phone requires the Demographics pencil, then the Contact tab in Edit Current Patient, then Save, after which the saved value must be re-read on the Dashboard Contact tab. The Demographics panel heading and its pencil are above the panel's detail rows: a large scroll from the top of the Dashboard can scroll the heading itself above the top of the screen while leaving the detail rows visible, so scroll part-way toward Demographics, check whether the heading is in view, and only scroll further if it is not yet visible. The Demographics Who, Contact, Choices tab bar and heading are likewise above the Who detail rows: a large scroll from the top of the Dashboard can scroll that heading and tab bar above the top of the screen while leaving the Who detail rows such as DOB, Birth Sex and External ID visible and readable, so when reading Demographics scroll only part-way, check whether those detail rows themselves are in view, scroll further only if they are not yet visible, and do not require the heading or tab bar to be visible before reading detail rows that are already showing. On the Dashboard Contact tab, Home Phone is the top row above Mobile Phone: scrolling down after opening that tab can push Home Phone itself above the top of the screen while Mobile Phone stays visible at the top edge, so do not scroll after opening Contact; check that Home Phone is in view, and scroll back up if Mobile Phone shows without Home Phone above it, before reading the saved value. In the Edit Current Patient Contact form, Home Phone and Work Phone are on the same horizontal row, with the Home Phone input in the left-hand column and the Work Phone input in the right-hand column on that same row; the automatic read-back after typing can mistake the empty right-hand Work Phone box for the Home Phone box and report the entered value as empty even when the typed value is visibly present in the left-hand Home Phone box, so that read-back must not be relied on for this field: type with the read-back check skipped, explicitly target the left-hand box, and verify the shown value in that left-hand box with a separate check before saving. The Patient Finder table 'Search:' box at the top-right, to the right of the 'Show entries' control and above the 'Search by External ID' column box, filters the table as text is entered; its automatic read-back after typing with Enter can report the entered text as empty or missing even when the text is visibly present in that Search box and the table below has correctly filtered to matching rows, so that read-back must not be relied on for this field: type the last name with the read-back check skipped, then verify the shown value in that Search box and the filtered table with separate checks before opening any row. On the Issues page each Medical Problems or Medications title link is followed by a status word shown inside parentheses; that status must always be read as only the word inside the parentheses, with the parentheses themselves omitted, otherwise independent reads of the same row can disagree by returning the word alone, the word still wrapped in parentheses, or nothing. Clicking an Issues row's '>' expander flips that expander to a down-pointing arrow in a box, which itself shows the row is expanded, but when the row sits near the bottom of the screen its expanded detail is pushed below the bottom edge and is not visible on that same screenshot; after expanding, scroll down a little at a time to bring the detail into view before judging, and accept the flipped down-pointing expander as proof of expansion if the detail is still below the fold. A read_list that advances by a large scroll between screenshots can leap straight over one or more Issues rows or whole expanded Issues blocks, so those rows never appear fully on any single screenshot and are silently missing from the merged result even though the run otherwise completes; this is especially easy for closely packed collapsed Medications rows, including older inactive medication rows listed below the current medication, and for expanded blocks whose title must be seen together with its detail. Read both Issues lists with small, overlapping scroll steps and enough pages to reach the bottom, count every Medical Problems and Medications row whatever its parenthesised status, and do not stop at the first or current medication. The first, collapsed Issues pass asks too much of a single screenshot if it tries to read each row's parenthesised status as well as its title: a row that is fully readable on one scrolled page can be cut off at the top or bottom edge on an overlapping page, so its status, the 'Occurrence Unknown or N/A' text at the far right of the same line, or the parentheses around the status can be read differently from page to page and the same medication can disagree between pages even though its blue title is identical. So in that first collapsed pass identify each row only by its section and the exact blue title link text, ignoring the parenthesised status word and the far-right Occurrence text entirely; the status is read only later, in the expanded pass, from a block whose title row is completely on screen. Likewise, a collapsed row that is cut off at an edge is not a separate row and must not be entered with a guessed or partial title; it is entered once, under exactly the same title text, on the page where it is fully visible. The section heading above an Issues row can itself scroll off the top of the screen on an overlapping page while that same row is still fully visible, so if a list pass also asks for the section heading, the same row can be read with its section on one page and with no section, or a guessed different section, on the next page and the merged list then reports that row as read differently on two pages even though its blue title never changed. So in both Issues list passes identify and merge each row or expanded block by its exact blue title-link text alone and do not read a section field at all in either pass; whether a title belongs to Medical Problems or Medications is not needed to expand it or to merge it, and the expanded block's own detail and code distinguish a problem from a medication. In the collapsed pass the title is only the text shown in blue: the parenthesised status after it is shown in black, is not part of the blue link, and must never be appended to the title on any page. The expanded Issues pass likewise asks too much of a single screenshot if, as well as copying the visible title, status, labelled dates and comment, it also asks for separate fields derived or parsed out of that same visible text, such as a code re-extracted from inside the blue title or a quantity and days-supply re-extracted from inside the comment prose: on one overlapping page that derived value can be copied in full, on another page where the same block is partly lower on the screen it can be shortened, reformatted or recorded as not recorded, and the merged list then reports the same block as read differently on two pages even though its blue title never changed. Those derived values are already preserved verbatim in the copied title and comment, so the expanded pass must not record them as separate fields at all. An expanded block also counts as cut off, and must be skipped on that page, whenever any part of its expanded detail runs below the bottom edge or is clipped, even if its title row and status are completely visible: such a block can have its comment, or its last detail line, read in full on one page and truncated or as not recorded on another. It is entered once, with exactly the same title, on the overlapping page where its title row and its whole expanded detail, down to the end of its final detail or comment line, are completely visible above the bottom edge.

item.title: the full blue link text at the top of this expanded block, including any diagnosis code in parentheses for a medical problem or strength for a medication that is itself part of the blue link, but not including the separate black parenthesised status word that follows the blue link; copy this blue text exactly and do not extract, repeat or reformat any code or strength inside it as a separate field
item.status: only the single status word inside the separate parentheses immediately after the blue title link, not any code parentheses inside the link itself and not the far-right 'Occurrence' text on the same line; copy that word alone exactly as written, with no parentheses, brackets or other punctuation around it, and never leave it blank when those status parentheses are fully visible on that same title row; if the title row is cut off so those status parentheses are not fully visible, do not guess it here - that block will be read on the next page instead
item.start_date: the begin or start date shown in the expanded detail directly below this title, beside its begin/start date label; if no begin or start date label is shown anywhere in this block's fully visible detail, say not recorded - a Last Modified date is not a begin or start date and a date from the next block below is not this block's date
item.end_date: the end date shown in the expanded detail directly below this title, beside its end date label; if no end date label is shown anywhere in this block's fully visible detail, say not recorded - a Last Modified date is not an end date and a date from the next block below is not this block's date
item.comment: the full comment text shown in the expanded detail directly below this title, beside a Comments label or in the Comments column, copied exactly and verbatim including any wording about a new order, quantities, supply or stopping; if no comment is shown in this block's fully visible detail, say not recorded. Do not parse, extract or summarise any number or phrase out of this comment into a separate field - the verbatim comment itself is the record

steps.where: Only expanded blocks under Medical Problems and Medications whose title row, including its blue link and the parenthesised status word after it, is completely on screen AND whose entire expanded detail directly below it is completely visible above the bottom edge of the screen, down to the end of its final detail or comment line, even if that detail shows only Last Modified and Comments with no begin, start or end date labels - in that case still count the block and record the missing dates as not recorded. Identify and merge each block by its exact blue title text alone; do not read or record a section heading for the block, because that heading can scroll off the top of an overlapping page while the block is still visible and must not make the same block read differently between pages, and do not record any separate field derived from the title or comment, such as a code extracted from the title or a quantity or days-supply extracted from the comment, because those are already preserved verbatim in the title and comment and deriving them can differ between pages. Count every such fully visible expanded block whatever its status, including any inactive, stopped or otherwise non-current medication blocks below the current medication, and keep each distinct title as its own block. Do not count Health Concerns, Allergies, 'None' rows, collapsed rows with no detail below them, or a block cut off at the bottom or top edge whose title, status, detail or final comment line is only partly visible or runs below the bottom edge or under the bottom scrollbar - such a cut-off block will be read in full, under exactly the same blue title and with exactly the same fields, on the next, closely overlapping scrolled page instead, and must not be entered on this page with a truncated comment, a missing date, or a guessed field.
